clauses.reason: Enacting words: the President acts under the Constitution and laws and orders what follows. The lead carries no command of its own and ends with section 1. First end of section 1: 2025-08-13 (signing on August 13, 2025).

Section 1 revokes the target order. The order states no effective date, so the revocation is read as taking effect on signing, August 13, 2025; that is a reading of the heading and signature block, not express wording, and the alternative dates are the filing date (August 18, 2025) and the printing date (August 19, 2025). The revocation is a one-time act; once made it had nothing further to command. Quoted words: "Competition in the American Economy), is hereby revoked.". Actor: the order itself; no later act was needed. The surviving consequence, that the target order stays revoked, is recorded under savings.

This general provision says nothing in the order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the matters in its items (i) and (ii); it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-08-13 (signing on August 13, 2025).

Item (i) of the non-derogation provision preserves the authority granted by law to an executive department or agency, or the head thereof; it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-08-13 (signing on August 13, 2025).

Item (ii) of the non-derogation provision preserves the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals; it is a rule of construction. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-08-13 (signing on August 13, 2025).

This general provision says the order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and subject to the availability of appropriations; it conditions how the order is carried out. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-08-13 (signing on August 13, 2025).

This general provision states that the order is not intended to, and does not, create any right or benefit enforceable at law or in equity against the United States or others; it states the order's effect. It is not a command and operates only alongside the revocation in section 1, so it ends when that act was complete, 2025-08-13 (signing on August 13, 2025).

Section 2(d) provides that the costs for publication of this order shall be borne by the Department of Justice. It allocates one cost, the cost of publishing the order, which the held Federal Register text shows was published on August 19, 2025 (90 FR 40227). The clause is read as spent on that publication date because publication is the event whose cost it allocates; no held source gives the date any bill was paid, so that reading is disclosed. This is the latest first end in the order, so it fixes the whole-order end at 2025-08-19, six days after the revocation in section 1 took effect.

The heading, number, title (Revocation of Executive Order on Competition) and date agree with the census register. Text and inventory: I read the whole held text; it is section 1 (revocation) and section 2 (general provisions, with a publication-cost provision in 2(d)), and the dossier's clause inventory matches those paragraphs and is complete. Lifecycle: the only operative command is the revocation of Executive Order 14036 of July 9, 2021 (Promoting Competition in the American Economy). It is a one-time act that was complete at signing on August 13, 2025, so section 1 and the clauses that operate alongside it end on 2025-08-13, and the publication-cost provision in section 2(d) ends on 2025-08-19, which is the latest first end and the whole-order end. No later instrument names this order: the packet's lookup of held order texts for its number lists only its own Federal Register text and the dossier's later-event chain is empty.

The surviving consequence is that Executive Order 14036 of July 9, 2021 (Promoting Competition in the American Economy) stays revoked, which is an accrued effect of the completed act and not a continuing command of this order; the held sources show no open claim.
